items.stem: Define the term “heterotrophic nutrition”.
items.answer: A mode of nutrition in which an organism depends on others for its organic food.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a mode of nutrition in which an organism depends on others for its organic food.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the history of classification and Whittaker's five kingdom system is correct?
items.answer: Aristotle classified plants into trees, shrubs and herbs.
items.markingKey: (a) Aristotle classified plants into trees, shrubs and herbs. The other statements are false. Linnaeus proposed the two kingdom system; Whittaker proposed five kingdoms. Fungi form a separate kingdom because of their heterotrophic nutrition and chitinous cell wall. Protists are unicellular eukaryotes.
options: Aristotle classified plants into trees, shrubs and herbs.
All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.
Whittaker proposed the two kingdom classification.
In the five kingdom system, fungi are placed in Kingdom Plantae.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The two kingdom system did not distinguish between eukaryotes and prokaryotes.
Reason (R): In the five kingdom system, fungi are placed in Kingdom Plantae.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Fungi form a separate kingdom because of their heterotrophic nutrition and chitinous cell wall.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.”
items.answer: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes.

items.stem: Compare Protista and Fungi on any three points.
items.answer: Protista: cell wall present in some; photosynthetic or heterotrophic; eukaryotic cell structure. Fungi: eukaryotic; multicellular or loose tissue (except yeast); heterotrophic (saprophytic or parasitic).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. Protista – cell wall present in some; photosynthetic or heterotrophic; eukaryotic cell structure; Fungi – eukaryotic; multicellular or loose tissue (except yeast); heterotrophic (saprophytic or parasitic).

items.stem:
A kingdom in Whittaker's system has these characteristics: heterotrophic (holozoic); no cell wall; eukaryotic.
(i) Identify the kingdom. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were Protista? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Animalia (ii) tissue, organ or organ system level of organisation (iii) photosynthetic or heterotrophic; unicellular
items.markingKey: (i) Animalia – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: tissue, organ or organ system level of organisation – 1 mark. (iii) for Protista: eukaryotic cell structure; unicellular; cell wall present in some – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between Monera and Animalia on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A kingdom in Whittaker's system has these characteristics: prokaryotic cell structure. Identify the kingdom – Monera or Animalia? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Monera: prokaryotic cell structure; unicellular; cell wall non-cellulosic (polysaccharide and amino acid). Animalia: eukaryotic; tissue, organ or organ system level of organisation; no cell wall. (b) Monera.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: Monera; 1 mark: “prokaryotic cell structure” is a feature of Monera.

items.stem: A kingdom in Whittaker's system has these characteristics: unicellular; prokaryotic cell structure. Identify the kingdom. Give a reason.
items.answer: Monera
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Monera; 1 mark: the features unicellular; prokaryotic cell structure are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Why was the two kingdom system of classification replaced by the five kingdom system?
items.answer: The two kingdom system did not distinguish prokaryotes from eukaryotes, unicellular from multicellular or photosynthetic from non-photosynthetic organisms; fungi, bacteria and algae were all called plants. Whittaker used cell structure, nutrition, body organisation, reproduction and phylogeny.
items.markingKey: 1 mark limitation; 1 mark new criteria.

items.stem: A kingdom in Whittaker's system has these characteristics: multicellular or loose tissue (except yeast); heterotrophic (saprophytic or parasitic). Identify the kingdom.
items.answer: Fungi
items.markingKey: (a) Fungi: multicellular or loose tissue (except yeast); heterotrophic (saprophytic or parasitic).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The two kingdom classification was found inadequate.
Reason (R): It placed prokaryotes and eukaryotes, unicellular and multicellular, photosynthetic and non-photosynthetic organisms together.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Major differences were ignored.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Give three limitations of the two kingdom classification.
items.answer: It did not distinguish eukaryotes from prokaryotes; unicellular from multicellular organisms; photosynthetic (green algae) from non-photosynthetic organisms (fungi); it placed fungi and bacteria in Plantae.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for any three limitations.

items.stem: What is meant by “mycoplasma”?
items.answer: Organisms that completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: organisms that completely lack a cell wall and are the smallest living cells known.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as cyanobacterium or archaebacterium: Nostoc, Anabaena, methanogens, Oscillatoria.
items.answer: Nostoc – cyanobacterium; Anabaena – cyanobacterium; methanogens – archaebacterium; Oscillatoria – cyanobacterium.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Nostoc – cyanobacterium; Anabaena – cyanobacterium; methanogens – archaebacterium; Oscillatoria – cyanobacterium.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a protozoan?
items.answer: Fuligo
items.markingKey: (b) Fuligo is a slime mould, not a protozoan.

items.stem: An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: heterotrophs living as predators or parasites; four major groups: amoeboid, flagellated, ciliated, sporozoans; include Amoeba, Paramoecium and Plasmodium. Identify the group it belongs to. Give a reason.
items.answer: Protozoans
items.markingKey: 1 mark: protozoans; 1 mark: the features heterotrophs living as predators or parasites; four major groups: amoeboid, flagellated, ciliated, sporozoans; include Amoeba, Paramoecium and Plasmodium are characteristic of it.

items.stem: An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse; mostly marine and photosynthetic. Identify the group it belongs to.
items.answer: dinoflagellates
items.markingKey: (d) Dinoflagellates: two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse; mostly marine and photosynthetic.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Monera and Kingdom Protista is incorrect?
items.answer: Trypanosoma, which causes sleeping sickness, is an amoeboid protozoan.
items.markingKey: (d) The incorrect statement is “Trypanosoma, which causes sleeping sickness, is an amoeboid protozoan.” Correct form: Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan.
options: Mycoplasma can survive without oxygen and many are pathogenic.
Red dinoflagellates such as Gonyaulax cause red tides.
Diatoms have left behind large deposits of cell wall material called diatomaceous earth.
Trypanosoma, which causes sleeping sickness, is an amoeboid protozoan.

items.stem:
A pond in a village near Kanpur turned green with a thick scum after fertiliser run-off from nearby fields. A microscope showed filaments with some larger, thick-walled cells.
(i) Which group of organisms forms such blooms? (1 mark)
(ii) Name the larger thick-walled cells and give their function. (1 mark)
(iii) Name two genera that have these cells and explain why such ponds become foul smelling. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae). (ii) Heterocysts; fix atmospheric nitrogen. (iii) Nostoc, Anabaena; the bloom dies and decomposes, depleting oxygen and releasing foul gases.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between chrysophytes and euglenoids on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: chief producers in the oceans. Identify the group it belongs to – chrysophytes or euglenoids? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Chrysophytes: cell walls form two overlapping shells; cell walls embedded with silica; chief producers in the oceans. Euglenoids: mostly fresh water; protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall; two flagella, one short and one long. (b) Chrysophytes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: chrysophytes; 1 mark: “chief producers in the oceans” is a feature of chrysophytes.

items.stem: Which term describes the protein-rich layer that makes the body of euglenoids flexible?
items.answer: pellicle
items.markingKey: (c) Pellicle: the protein-rich layer that makes the body of euglenoids flexible.

items.stem: Which of the following is an archaebacterium?
items.answer: halophiles
items.markingKey: (c) Halophiles is an archaebacterium; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following is a chrysophyte?
items.answer: diatoms
items.markingKey: (d) Diatoms is a chrysophyte; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Diatoms are the chief consumers in the oceans.”
items.answer: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Monera and Kingdom Protista is correct?
items.answer: Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, is a sporozoan.
items.markingKey: (b) Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, is a sporozoan. The other statements are false. Euglenoids have no cell wall; they have a protein-rich pellicle. Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans. Trypanosoma is a flagellated protozoan.
options: Trypanosoma, which causes sleeping sickness, is an amoeboid protozoan.
Plasmodium, the malarial parasite, is a sporozoan.
Euglenoids have a cell wall made of cellulose.
Diatoms are the chief consumers in the oceans.

items.stem: Give three differences between protozoans and chrysophytes.
items.answer: Protozoans: include Amoeba, Paramoecium and Plasmodium; heterotrophs living as predators or parasites; believed to be primitive relatives of animals. Chrysophytes: cell walls embedded with silica; mostly photosynthetic, found in fresh and marine water; chief producers in the oceans.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. protozoans – include Amoeba, Paramoecium and Plasmodium; heterotrophs living as predators or parasites; believed to be primitive relatives of animals; chrysophytes – cell walls embedded with silica; mostly photosynthetic, found in fresh and marine water; chief producers in the oceans.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Slime moulds can survive unfavourable conditions for many years.
Reason (R): Under unfavourable conditions the plasmodium forms fruiting bodies bearing spores with true walls.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Spores are extremely resistant.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Describe the four major groups of protozoans with one example each. How are protists different from monerans?
items.answer: Amoeboid – pseudopodia, e.g. Amoeba, Entamoeba; flagellated – flagella, free-living or parasitic, e.g. Trypanosoma (sleeping sickness); ciliated – cilia, gullet, e.g. Paramoecium; sporozoans – infectious spore-like stage, e.g. Plasmodium (malaria). Protists are eukaryotic with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; monerans are prokaryotic.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each for four groups; 1 mark difference.

items.stem: What is meant by “saprophytes”?
items.answer: Organisms that absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: organisms that absorb soluble organic matter from dead substrates.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as deuteromycete or phycomycete: Colletotrichum, Alternaria, Mucor, Trichoderma.
items.answer: Colletotrichum – deuteromycete; Alternaria – deuteromycete; Mucor – phycomycete; Trichoderma – deuteromycete.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Colletotrichum – deuteromycete; Alternaria – deuteromycete; Mucor – phycomycete; Trichoderma – deuteromycete.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): In basidiomycetes, sex organs are absent and plasmogamy occurs by fusion of two vegetative or somatic cells.
Reason (R): Phycomycetes have septate mycelium.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A fungus has these features: branched septate mycelium; fruiting bodies called basidiocarps; asexual spores generally not found; vegetative reproduction by fragmentation common. Identify its class. Give a reason.
items.answer: Basidiomycetes
items.markingKey: 1 mark: basidiomycetes; 1 mark: the features branched septate mycelium; fruiting bodies called basidiocarps; asexual spores generally not found; vegetative reproduction by fragmentation common are characteristic of it.

items.stem: A fungus has these features: asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores; septate and branched mycelium. Identify its class.
items.answer: ascomycetes
items.markingKey: (d) Ascomycetes: asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores; septate and branched mycelium.

items.stem:
Kavya kept a slice of moist bread in a closed box for a week. It developed a white cottony growth with tiny black dots.
(i) Name the organism likely to have grown. (1 mark)
(ii) To which class does it belong and what is the nature of its mycelium? (1 mark)
(iii) What are the black dots, and how does this fungus obtain nutrition? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Rhizopus (bread mould) or Mucor. (ii) Phycomycetes; aseptate, coenocytic mycelium. (iii) Sporangia containing asexual spores; saprophytic – absorbs soluble organic matter from the bread.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of events in ascomycetes and basidiomycetes: dikaryon (n + n) stage, plasmogamy, karyogamy, meiosis. Give a reason.
items.answer: plasmogamy → dikaryon (n + n) stage → karyogamy → meiosis
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order plasmogamy → dikaryon (n + n) stage → karyogamy → meiosis; 1 mark for the reason: An intervening dikaryotic phase follows plasmogamy.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between deuteromycetes and ascomycetes on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A fungus has these features: reproduce only by asexual spores called conidia. Identify its class – deuteromycetes or ascomycetes? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Deuteromycetes: only asexual or vegetative phases known; septate and branched mycelium; reproduce only by asexual spores called conidia. Ascomycetes: septate and branched mycelium; asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores; sexual spores are ascospores produced endogenously in asci. (b) Deuteromycetes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: deuteromycetes; 1 mark: “reproduce only by asexual spores called conidia” is a feature of deuteromycetes.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a phycomycete?
items.answer: Puccinia (rust fungus)
items.markingKey: (d) Puccinia (rust fungus) is a basidiomycete, not a phycomycete.

items.stem: Which term describes the fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes?
items.answer: plasmogamy
items.markingKey: (c) Plasmogamy: the fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about Kingdom Fungi is correct?
items.answer: The cell wall of fungi is made of chitin and polysaccharides.
items.markingKey: (d) The cell wall of fungi is made of chitin and polysaccharides. The other statements are false. Their mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Ascospores are produced endogenously in sac-like asci; basidiospores are exogenous on basidia. Yeast is unicellular.
options: Ascospores are produced exogenously on basidia.
The cell wall of fungi is made of chitin and polysaccharides.

items.stem: What is meant by “lichens”?
items.answer: Symbiotic associations between algae and fungi.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: symbiotic associations between algae and fungi.

items.stem: Explain the term “capsid”.
items.answer: The protein coat of a virus, made of small subunits called capsomeres.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the protein coat of a virus, made of small subunits called capsomeres.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about viruses, viroids, prions and lichens is correct?
items.answer: Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.
items.markingKey: (a) Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA. The other statements are false. Viroids are free RNA without a protein coat; their RNA is of low molecular weight. Prions are abnormally folded proteins. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas and serve as pollution indicators.
options: Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.
Viroids have a protein coat but lack RNA.
Lichens grow luxuriantly in polluted cities.

items.stem: An infectious agent or association has these features: free RNA without a protein coat; discovered by T.O. Diener. Identify it. Give a reason.
items.answer: A viroid
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a viroid; 1 mark: the features free RNA without a protein coat; discovered by T.O. Diener are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Distinguish between a prion and a lichen on any three points.
items.answer: A prion: causes Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease in humans; causes BSE in cattle; abnormally folded protein. A lichen: association of an alga and a fungus; do not grow in polluted areas; fungal component is the mycobiont.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each of three correct, paired points of difference, e.g. a prion – causes Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease in humans; causes BSE in cattle; abnormally folded protein; a lichen – association of an alga and a fungus; do not grow in polluted areas; fungal component is the mycobiont.

items.stem:
Leaves of a tobacco crop near Guntur showed a patchy mosaic of light and dark green. Sap from these leaves passed through a bacteria-proof filter still infected healthy plants.
(i) What kind of agent causes this disease? (1 mark)
(ii) Who first showed this and what name did Beijerinck give the infectious fluid? (1 mark)
(iii) Give two reasons why such agents are not placed in any of the five kingdoms. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) A virus – tobacco mosaic virus. (ii) D.J. Ivanowsky; Contagium vivum fluidum. (iii) They are non-cellular; they are inert outside a host and show life only inside living cells (no metabolism of their own).
items.markingKey: (i) 1 (ii) ½ + ½ (iii) 1 + 1.

items.stem: Which of the following is a disease caused by a virus?
items.answer: small pox
items.markingKey: (a) Small pox is a disease caused by a virus; the others are not.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Prions are infectious nucleic acids.”
items.answer: Prions are abnormally folded proteins.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Prions are abnormally folded proteins.

items.stem: Define the term “bacteriophage”.
items.answer: A virus that infects bacteria, usually with double-stranded DNA.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a virus that infects bacteria, usually with double-stranded DNA.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as disease caused by a virus or disease caused by a prion: influenza, Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease, bovine spongiform encephalopathy (mad cow disease).
items.answer: influenza – disease caused by a virus; Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease – disease caused by a prion; bovine spongiform encephalopathy (mad cow disease) – disease caused by a prion.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: influenza – disease caused by a virus; Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease – disease caused by a prion; bovine spongiform encephalopathy (mad cow disease) – disease caused by a prion.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a lichen and a prion on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An infectious agent or association has these features: algal component is the phycobiont. Identify it – a lichen or a prion? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A lichen: association of an alga and a fungus; algal component is the phycobiont; fungal component is the mycobiont. A prion: abnormally folded protein; similar in size to viruses; causes BSE in cattle. (b) A lichen.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a lichen; 1 mark: “algal component is the phycobiont” is a feature of a lichen.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Ascospores are produced exogenously on basidia.”
items.answer: Ascospores are produced endogenously in sac-like asci; basidiospores are exogenous on basidia.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Ascospores are produced endogenously in sac-like asci; basidiospores are exogenous on basidia.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between slime moulds and chrysophytes on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: chief producers in the oceans. Identify the group it belongs to – slime moulds or chrysophytes? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Slime moulds: saprophytic protists; aggregate to form a plasmodium under suitable conditions; form fruiting bodies with spores in unfavourable conditions. Chrysophytes: cell walls form two overlapping shells; cell walls embedded with silica; chief producers in the oceans. (b) Chrysophytes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: chrysophytes; 1 mark: “chief producers in the oceans” is a feature of chrysophytes.

items.stem: Which of the following is a deuteromycete?
items.answer: Trichoderma
items.markingKey: (d) Trichoderma is a deuteromycete; the others are not.

items.stem: What is meant by “the two kingdom classification”?
items.answer: The system of Linnaeus that grouped all organisms into Plantae and Animalia.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the system of Linnaeus that grouped all organisms into Plantae and Animalia.

items.stem: An infectious agent or association has these features: genetic material is either RNA or DNA, never both; inert outside a host cell. Identify it.
items.answer: a virus
items.markingKey: (b) A virus: genetic material is either RNA or DNA, never both; inert outside a host cell.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as protozoan or slime mould: Plasmodium, Trypanosoma, Fuligo, Amoeba.
items.answer: Plasmodium – protozoan; Trypanosoma – protozoan; Fuligo – slime mould; Amoeba – protozoan.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Plasmodium – protozoan; Trypanosoma – protozoan; Fuligo – slime mould; Amoeba – protozoan.

items.stem: Give two differences between Protista and Monera.
items.answer: Protista: photosynthetic or heterotrophic; eukaryotic cell structure. Monera: cell wall non-cellulosic (polysaccharide and amino acid); autotrophic or heterotrophic.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. Protista – photosynthetic or heterotrophic; eukaryotic cell structure; Monera – cell wall non-cellulosic (polysaccharide and amino acid); autotrophic or heterotrophic.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a virus and a lichen on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An infectious agent or association has these features: association of an alga and a fungus. Identify it – a virus or a lichen? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A virus: nucleoprotein particle; genetic material is either RNA or DNA, never both; protein coat (capsid) of capsomeres. A lichen: association of an alga and a fungus; algal component is the phycobiont; fungal component is the mycobiont. (b) A lichen.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a lichen; 1 mark: “association of an alga and a fungus” is a feature of a lichen.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as archaebacterium or cyanobacterium: thermoacidophiles, methanogens, halophiles, Oscillatoria.
items.answer: thermoacidophiles – archaebacterium; methanogens – archaebacterium; halophiles – archaebacterium; Oscillatoria – cyanobacterium.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: thermoacidophiles – archaebacterium; methanogens – archaebacterium; halophiles – archaebacterium; Oscillatoria – cyanobacterium.

items.stem: Give two differences between basidiomycetes and ascomycetes.
items.answer: Basidiomycetes: fruiting bodies called basidiocarps; basidiospores produced exogenously on the basidium. Ascomycetes: fruiting bodies called ascocarps; septate and branched mycelium.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. basidiomycetes – fruiting bodies called basidiocarps; basidiospores produced exogenously on the basidium; ascomycetes – fruiting bodies called ascocarps; septate and branched mycelium.

items.stem: Explain the term “diatoms”.
items.answer: Chrysophytes whose cell walls form two thin overlapping shells fitting together like a soap box.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: chrysophytes whose cell walls form two thin overlapping shells fitting together like a soap box.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Viroids have a protein coat but lack RNA.
Reason (R): D.J. Ivanowsky found that certain microbes causing mosaic disease of tobacco were smaller than bacteria.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Viroids are free RNA without a protein coat; their RNA is of low molecular weight. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A kingdom in Whittaker's system has these characteristics: cell wall of cellulose; eukaryotic. Identify the kingdom. Give a reason.
items.answer: Plantae
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Plantae; 1 mark: the features cell wall of cellulose; eukaryotic are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between ascomycetes and phycomycetes on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A fungus has these features: aseptate, coenocytic mycelium. Identify its class – ascomycetes or phycomycetes? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Ascomycetes: septate and branched mycelium; asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores; sexual spores are ascospores produced endogenously in asci. Phycomycetes: aseptate, coenocytic mycelium; asexual zoospores or aplanospores produced endogenously in sporangia; zygospore formed by fusion of two gametes. (b) Phycomycetes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: phycomycetes; 1 mark: “aseptate, coenocytic mycelium” is a feature of phycomycetes.

items.stem: Which of the following is an archaebacterium?
items.answer: thermoacidophiles
items.markingKey: (b) Thermoacidophiles is an archaebacterium; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the history of classification and Whittaker's five kingdom system is incorrect?
items.answer: All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.
items.markingKey: (a) The incorrect statement is “All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.” Correct form: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes.
options: All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.
In the two kingdom system, bacteria, fungi and photosynthetic organisms were all placed in Plantae.
R.H. Whittaker proposed the five kingdom classification in 1969.

items.stem: Define the term “prion”.
items.answer: An abnormally folded protein that causes infectious neurological diseases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an abnormally folded protein that causes infectious neurological diseases.

items.stem:
An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: include Amoeba, Paramoecium and Plasmodium; believed to be primitive relatives of animals; four major groups: amoeboid, flagellated, ciliated, sporozoans.
(i) Identify the group it belongs to. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were dinoflagellates? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Protozoans (ii) heterotrophs living as predators or parasites (iii) mostly marine and photosynthetic; two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse
items.markingKey: (i) protozoans – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: heterotrophs living as predators or parasites – 1 mark. (iii) for dinoflagellates: mostly marine and photosynthetic; stiff cellulose plates on the cell wall; two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as ascomycete or phycomycete: Rhizopus, Albugo, Mucor, Penicillium.
items.answer: Rhizopus – phycomycete; Albugo – phycomycete; Mucor – phycomycete; Penicillium – ascomycete.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Rhizopus – phycomycete; Albugo – phycomycete; Mucor – phycomycete; Penicillium – ascomycete.

items.stem: Give two differences between slime moulds and chrysophytes.
items.answer: Slime moulds: saprophytic protists; aggregate to form a plasmodium under suitable conditions. Chrysophytes: cell walls embedded with silica; mostly photosynthetic, found in fresh and marine water.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. slime moulds – saprophytic protists; aggregate to form a plasmodium under suitable conditions; chrysophytes – cell walls embedded with silica; mostly photosynthetic, found in fresh and marine water.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Yeast is a multicellular fungus.”
items.answer: Yeast is unicellular.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Yeast is unicellular.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between chrysophytes and slime moulds on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: cell walls embedded with silica. Identify the group it belongs to – chrysophytes or slime moulds? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Chrysophytes: cell walls form two overlapping shells; cell walls embedded with silica; chief producers in the oceans. Slime moulds: saprophytic protists; aggregate to form a plasmodium under suitable conditions; form fruiting bodies with spores in unfavourable conditions. (b) Chrysophytes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: chrysophytes; 1 mark: “cell walls embedded with silica” is a feature of chrysophytes.

items.stem: Which of the following is an ascomycete?
items.answer: Aspergillus
items.markingKey: (c) Aspergillus is an ascomycete; the others are not.

items.stem: Define the term “the five kingdom classification”.
items.answer: The system proposed by R.H. Whittaker in 1969 with Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the system proposed by R.H. Whittaker in 1969 with Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

items.stem: An infectious agent or association has these features: RNA of low molecular weight; causes potato spindle tuber disease. Identify it.
items.answer: a viroid
items.markingKey: (b) A viroid: RNA of low molecular weight; causes potato spindle tuber disease.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as euglenoid or chrysophyte: desmids, diatoms, Euglena.
items.answer: desmids – chrysophyte; diatoms – chrysophyte; Euglena – euglenoid.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: desmids – chrysophyte; diatoms – chrysophyte; Euglena – euglenoid.

items.stem: Give two differences between Protista and Animalia.
items.answer: Protista: eukaryotic cell structure; cell wall present in some. Animalia: eukaryotic; heterotrophic (holozoic).
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. Protista – eukaryotic cell structure; cell wall present in some; Animalia – eukaryotic; heterotrophic (holozoic).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a prion and a viroid on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) An infectious agent or association has these features: RNA of low molecular weight. Identify it – a prion or a viroid? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A prion: abnormally folded protein; similar in size to viruses; causes BSE in cattle. A viroid: free RNA without a protein coat; RNA of low molecular weight; causes potato spindle tuber disease. (b) A viroid.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a viroid; 1 mark: “RNA of low molecular weight” is a feature of a viroid.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as cyanobacterium or archaebacterium: Anabaena, Nostoc, Oscillatoria, methanogens.
items.answer: Anabaena – cyanobacterium; Nostoc – cyanobacterium; Oscillatoria – cyanobacterium; methanogens – archaebacterium.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Anabaena – cyanobacterium; Nostoc – cyanobacterium; Oscillatoria – cyanobacterium; methanogens – archaebacterium.

items.stem: Give two differences between phycomycetes and ascomycetes.
items.answer: Phycomycetes: zygospore formed by fusion of two gametes; e.g. Mucor, Rhizopus, Albugo. Ascomycetes: fruiting bodies called ascocarps; asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. phycomycetes – zygospore formed by fusion of two gametes; e.g. Mucor, Rhizopus, Albugo; ascomycetes – fruiting bodies called ascocarps; asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores.

items.stem: Explain the term “pellicle”.
items.answer: The protein-rich layer that makes the body of euglenoids flexible.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the protein-rich layer that makes the body of euglenoids flexible.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Prions are infectious nucleic acids.
Reason (R): Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Prions are abnormally folded proteins. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A kingdom in Whittaker's system has these characteristics: eukaryotic cell structure; cell wall present in some; photosynthetic or heterotrophic. Identify the kingdom. Give a reason.
items.answer: Protista
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Protista; 1 mark: the features eukaryotic cell structure; cell wall present in some; photosynthetic or heterotrophic are characteristic of it.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between ascomycetes and basidiomycetes on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A fungus has these features: basidiospores produced exogenously on the basidium. Identify its class – ascomycetes or basidiomycetes? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Ascomycetes: septate and branched mycelium; asexual spores are conidia produced exogenously on conidiophores; sexual spores are ascospores produced endogenously in asci. Basidiomycetes: branched septate mycelium; asexual spores generally not found; vegetative reproduction by fragmentation common; basidiospores produced exogenously on the basidium. (b) Basidiomycetes.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: basidiomycetes; 1 mark: “basidiospores produced exogenously on the basidium” is a feature of basidiomycetes.

items.stem: Which of the following is an archaebacterium?
items.answer: methanogens
items.markingKey: (d) Methanogens is an archaebacterium; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the history of classification and Whittaker's five kingdom system is incorrect?
items.answer: All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.” Correct form: Protists are unicellular eukaryotes.
options: The two kingdom system did not distinguish between eukaryotes and prokaryotes.
All members of Kingdom Protista are multicellular.
Members of Kingdom Fungi are heterotrophic with cell walls made of chitin.

items.stem: What is meant by “viroid”?
items.answer: A free RNA infectious agent lacking a protein coat, discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a free RNA infectious agent lacking a protein coat, discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971.

items.stem:
An organism examined in the laboratory shows these features: chief producers in the oceans; cell walls embedded with silica; cell walls form two overlapping shells.
(i) Identify the group it belongs to. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were dinoflagellates? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Chrysophytes (ii) mostly photosynthetic, found in fresh and marine water (iii) may cause red tides; stiff cellulose plates on the cell wall
items.markingKey: (i) chrysophytes – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: mostly photosynthetic, found in fresh and marine water – 1 mark. (iii) for dinoflagellates: mostly marine and photosynthetic; stiff cellulose plates on the cell wall; two flagella, one longitudinal and one transverse – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as ascomycete or deuteromycete: Alternaria, Claviceps, Penicillium, yeast (Saccharomyces).
items.answer: Alternaria – deuteromycete; Claviceps – ascomycete; Penicillium – ascomycete; yeast (Saccharomyces) – ascomycete.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: Alternaria – deuteromycete; Claviceps – ascomycete; Penicillium – ascomycete; yeast (Saccharomyces) – ascomycete.

items.stem: Give two differences between protozoans and euglenoids.
items.answer: Protozoans: believed to be primitive relatives of animals; heterotrophs living as predators or parasites. Euglenoids: protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall; mostly fresh water.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. protozoans – believed to be primitive relatives of animals; heterotrophs living as predators or parasites; euglenoids – protein-rich pellicle instead of a cell wall; mostly fresh water.
